narration.text: Why the first interstellar visitor was already leaving.
ʻOumuamua was spotted in 2017, heading away from the Sun.
It was 33 million kilometres away when first seen.
It travels about 94,800 kilometres per hour in interstellar space.
It may be 100 to 1,000 metres long.
It showed no comet tail, so it was reclassified.
So visitors from other stars pass by, and we barely notice.
